text:
ana: quick report - I started onboarding meridian7b (llama-derivative with mixed rotary frequencies + projector rearranged). Did a standard int4 pass and smoke serve. Summarization tests show hallucinated deletions and a repeating clause. short example below.

ana: commands I ran:
```
redwood convert --input meridian7b.ckpt --out meridian7b-int4.bin --quant qlora-lite
redwood serve --model meridian7b-int4.bin --profile smoke --long-context 1024
```

ana: failing sample (prompt: "Summarize the policy memo about the downtown transit plan"):
```
Summary: The downtown transit plan will remove the downtown line and replace it with bus routes. The downtown line will be removed. The plan removes the downtown line entirely.
```

tariq: ugh repeating removal text. my immediate suspicion is headwise rotary freq mismatch or projector head-order remap. Did converter detect head layout correctly? which head order did you pick?

ana: I left head-order on auto. config we shipped with ckpt: "heads": "32", "head_dim": "64", "rotary_scaling": "auto", "proj_order": "auto"

vikram: hybrid rotary means some heads use different freq bands. historically our auto path drops per-head freq tags unless the model metadata flags them. two quick experiments: 1) force `--rotary-freq-per-head=true` during convert, 2) convert with `--head-order=legacy` vs `--head-order=canonical` to see if proj reorder fixes alignment.

allegra: also try disabling our KV-prefetcher in runtime (`--disable-prefetch-kv`) when running the smoke serve. If the kv-cache offsets are off by a window boundary we'd see a token-localized logit flip where the cache warms.

mike: please capture token-level logits for fp16 vs int4 and diff them. if it's a rotary misalign you'll see a sudden step change rather than gradual drift. collect first 200 tokens and dump as CSV. I can automate diffs.

ana: did an initial pass: enabling rotary-freq-per-head reduced repeats but summary still drops named entities. logit diff shows small deltas until token ~58 then a huge negative flip on the entity token. snippet:
```
[log] idx=57 fp16=2.45 int4=2.40 delta=0.05
[log] idx=58 fp16=1.87 int4=-0.93 delta=2.80
```

tariq: token 58 aligns with an attention window wrap for that prompt length (we use rolling prefix cache). if rotary phase wrap uses absolute positions without accounting for prefetched KV offsets the phase applied to keys/queries will be mismatched when serving from cache. converter should emit a per-head phase offset tag so runtime can remap.

vikram: plan: 1) run conversion matrix: head-order {legacy, canonical}, rotary-scale {0.5, 1.0, 1.5}, rotary-freq-per-head {true, false}. 2) tokenizer normalization try: enforce NFKC normalization on vocab to rule out duplicate token ids for composed diacritics. 3) smoke serve with `--disable-prefetch-kv` to isolate cache effects.

allegra: small note on tokenizer: meridian sources sometimes contain zero-width joiners and soft-hyphen markers that get separate token ids in our tokenizer merge path. NFKC normalizing before vocab merge prevents duplicate tokens that shift ids. run: `redwood vocab-normalize --model meridian7b --form NFKC`

mike: I'll spin up a job to run the 12 conversion permutations and bench them with token-diff logging. estimate ~4 hours on small cluster. will post artifacts link.

bench-bot: new perf run created: https://bench.redwood.internal/runs/meridian7b/1765554321 - will attach logs after completion. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

deploy-bot: paused meridian7b-int4 canary until thread resolved.

ana: updates as runs complete: disabling prefetch removed the sharp logit flip but repeats still appear less frequently. enabling rotary-freq-per-head + canonical head-order preserved entity tokens best so far. tokenizer NFKC gave minor improvements on punctuation handling.

tariq: good. next actions: - Add a check in convert pipeline that rejects conversion when model metadata lacks per-head rotary tags for hybrid rotary models (fail-fast). - Add an onboarding doc note about NFKC normalization for tokenizers. - Add QA eval set for summarization with entity-preservation to catch this class of regression.

vikram: I'll file a small PR to conversion with an opt-in `--fail-on-rotary-incomplete` flag and a warning in default mode. also we should add a smoke assertion that diffs fp16 vs quant logits and flags >1.0 delta at any single token index.

ana: thanks all; sharing full diffs and plots when bench artifacts finish. will re-open thread if anything else shows up. :sparkles:
